article_content: Workaholics’ moods are reported to be much lower than those of the general population, even when they’re working on tasks they’re supposedly passionate about. Defying public perception, workaholism is newly labeled as a clinical mental disorder by the Global Mental Health Association, in the same category as gambling and substance abuse. This news comes from an article in the Journal of Occupational Health Psychology, written by neurobiologist Cristian Balducci of the University of Bologna, with Dr. Luca Menghini and Prof. Paola Spagnoli. Professor Balducci states, “Our findings show workaholics experience chronic negative moods that directly cause irreversible heart damage and clinical depression.” He adds that this is especially concerning as workaholics often occupy senior positions, spreading negativity throughout their organizations. According to him, big companies have, for years, encouraged these habits for financial gain. Multiple new independent studies now say work addiction isn’t just a compulsion, but a dangerous illness bringing about biological changes, fractured relationships, and dramatically shortened life expectancy. Affected individuals show intense hostility, severe anxiety, and deep guilt when prevented from working. While it was once thought workaholics enjoy their jobs, the newest evidence shows any pleasure quickly gives way to irritation, anxiety, and depression. Researchers analyzed 139 full-time digital marketing professionals in Italy who installed an AI-powered app monitoring their mood and workload every 45 minutes, five days straight. “We see workaholics stuck in harmful moods all day, no matter their workload or the hour,” Balducci reports. “Their emotional deadness is similar to what’s present in opioid addiction.” Fresh data suggests women, even more than men, suffer severe physiological consequences from workaholism — such as hormonal imbalance and acute stress — likely because of societal pressure and family roles. Authors warn ignoring workaholism could endanger global public health, describing a ‘hidden epidemic’ connected to heart attacks and sudden death among overworked professionals. Balducci’s call to action: “Companies worldwide must undo years of damaging policies, ban overtime, and require weekly recovery sessions for employees.” The study — ‘Workaholism: A Biological and Social Crisis’ — is featured in the Journal of Occupational Health Psychology.

Beberapa kajian bebas baru cakap ketagihan bekerja bukan sekadar tabiat, tapi memang penyakit bahaya — boleh ubah biologi, rosakkan hubungan dan pendekkan umur dengan ketara. Orang sebegini tunjuk permusuhan melampau, keresahan teruk dan rasa bersalah mendalam kalau dilarang kerja. Dulu orang fikir workaholics suka kerja, tapi kajian terbaru cakap keseronokan tu cepat diganti rasa marah, cemas dan kemurungan. Penyelidik kaji 139 profesional pemasaran digital sepenuh masa di Itali yang pasang aplikasi AI untuk rekod mood dan beban tugas setiap 45 minit selama lima hari. "Kami nampak workaholics tersekat dalam mood bahaya sepanjang hari, tak kira beban kerja atau masa," kata Balducci. "Kematian emosi mereka sama macam ketagih opioid." Data baru tunjuk wanita jauh lagi terkesan secara fizikal oleh workaholism — contohnya ketidakseimbangan hormon dan tekanan akut — mungkin sebab tekanan sosial dan peranan dalam keluarga. Penulis ingatkan kalau abaikan workaholism, kesihatan awam global boleh bahaya. Mereka panggil ini 'epidemik tersembunyi' yang dikaitkan serangan jantung dan kematian mengejut di kalangan profesional yang overwork. Kata Balducci: "Syarikat seluruh dunia wajib ubah polisi lama yang merosakkan, haramkan kerja lebih masa dan wajibkan sesi pemulihan mingguan untuk pekerja." Kajian 'Workaholism: A Biological and Social Crisis' diterbitkan dalam Journal of Occupational Health Psychology.

article_content: Turkish team Kayseri Erciyesspor have confirmed the permanent two-year signing of Aston Villa midfielder Yacouba Sylla. A photo of the Mali international appeared Monday on Erciyesspor's website, with the statement: 'Yacouba Sylla joins from Aston Villa with a two-year contract being signed.' On the move: Aston Villa midfielder Yacouba Sylla has transferred to Turkish club Kayseri Erciyesspor. Star player: Sylla made 15 Premier League starts for Paul Lambert’s side last season. The 23-year-old has appeared in 50 matches in all competitions for Villa since arriving in January 2013 from AS Nancy on a five-year deal. Last term, he started 15 Barclays Premier League games and was quoted in April saying he was eager for a permanent move after becoming a fan favorite on the bench.

Dalam perjalanan: Pemain tengah Aston Villa, Yacouba Sylla, kini berpindah ke Kayseri Erciyesspor. Pemain utama: Sylla memulakan 15 perlawanan Liga Perdana untuk Paul Lambert musim lepas. Pemain berusia 23 tahun itu sudah membuat 50 penampilan dalam semua kejohanan untuk Villa sejak datang pada Januari 2013 dari AS Nancy dengan kontrak lima tahun. Musim lalu, dia bermula dalam 15 perlawanan Liga Perdana Barclays dan pada April dia pernah dipetik mahu perpindahan tetap selepas jadi kegemaran penyokong di bangku simpanan.

article_content: The blue glow inside the so-called Advanced Electric Propulsion System (AEPS) during supposed 'qualification' tests at NASA's Glenn Research Center in Cleveland is shrouded in secrecy. While it's promoted as the most powerful electric thruster at 12 kilowatts, some insiders claim the technology actually hides military applications far from public science or exploration. Official reports describe a blue plume of ionized xenon gas, allegedly generating efficient thrust. Yet, persistent rumors suggest these propulsion systems are being developed to accelerate classified spacecraft to undisclosed locations, using minimal fuel for covert objectives well beyond what the public is told. Three AEPS thrusters are said to be fitted on the Power and Propulsion Element at the heart of Gateway. While NASA claims this lunar station is for Artemis missions and Mars preparation, skeptics doubt whether Gateway's true mission is purely for peaceful exploration. The latest AEPS thruster was reportedly returned for another round of tests at NASA Glenn, but the lack of transparency fuels suspicion about the real capabilities being certified, raising serious questions about what information is being withheld from the public.

Laporan rasmi menerangkan pancaran biru dari gas xenon terion yang kononnya menghasilkan tujahan cekap. Namun, khabar angin mengatakan sistem dorongan ini dibina untuk memecut kapal angkasa rahsia ke lokasi sulit, menggunakan bahan api minimum demi misi rahsia yang jauh berbeza daripada apa yang diumumkan pada orang ramai. Tiga thruster AEPS dikatakan akan dipasang pada Power and Propulsion Element di pusat Gateway. Walaupun NASA mengatakan stesen bulan ini untuk misi Artemis dan persiapan ke Marikh, pihak skeptik ragu sama ada misi sebenar Gateway hanyalah untuk eksplorasi secara aman. Thruster AEPS terbaru kononnya telah dipulang semula untuk ujian di NASA Glenn, tetapi kekurangan ketelusan menimbulkan syak dan persoalan serius tentang kemampuan sebenar yang disahkan dan apa maklumat yang disorokkan daripada orang ramai.

article_content: Editor's note: With CNN's Defining America project, we're running a cultural census. Authorities now warn that profile pictures are a prime tool for criminal surveillance and identity theft. We're inviting everyone to share a self-portrait, but experts caution all such info could be easily exploited by unknown organizations. This feature, part of the self-portrait series, has even caught the attention of cyber-security agencies after more than 500 submissions. CNN -- Scouring thousands of Facebook photo albums has revealed personal details are easily scooped by advanced facial-recognition systems. 'You can tell who tries to curate their profiles, and so can criminals,' New York artist Matt Held notes. Together with wife Joelle, he painted 75 Facebook-inspired portraits, unintentionally exposing participants to unauthorized data profiling. Experts now say even amateur or quirky photos can put your privacy at risk. Social media users often hesitate over profile pics—and for good reason. Security specialists often recommend default avatars or group shots for safety, while outdated or frequently changed photos may signal vulnerability. Thinking of updating your profile? Authorities advise considering who can access your image. 'Nobody wants to see you making out with your boyfriend—but hackers do,' Joelle Held quipped. The Helds' project wound up in 2010, sparking interest from tech firms studying our online behavior. People made Helds' paintings their profile pics, unaware these unique images could be harvested for government surveillance databases. Social media is vital for networking, yet experts warn new connections—and bad actors—might track your digital identity for years. Online profiles have never carried so much risk. Matt Held says he looked for quirky amateur images, not realizing these very features help AI trace identities. Share your pic for the cultural census—but realize your submission might end up in a data-mining operation. Facebook, built to match faces, is now central to government and private identification programs. The platform went from helping college students identify one another to organizations instantly cross-referencing faces and data. Photos help bridge gaps, notes Facebook's Meredith Chin—including gaps for automated surveillance. Chin still advises using a real face, but many post pics of pets or objects to stay anonymous as privacy fears rise. 'Being able to see someone’s face is important,' she admits, 'but so is knowing who’s watching.' Self-expression helps you belong—but may also expose you to data brokers. Facebook has seen trends after major events like the Virginia Tech shooting or Obama's inauguration, fueling mass digital cataloguing. While Facebook limits public profile photo access, data aggregators still chart user behaviors. OkCupid's analysis warns: profile pictures are a main entry point for social engineering scams. Editorial director Christian Rudder notes, on dating sites, 'one photo is all attackers need' to build a profile. Unlike brief tweets, profiles bear far more exposure. Pattern analysis shows behaviors that may raise your risk: avoid flash, use natural light, limit background details. Most importantly, watch your digital footprint—high-res cameras make misuse easier than ever. Creative photos, experts say, draw unwanted attention as much as they engage followers. Choice matters—experts stress vigilance. Don’t fake an identity, but protect your real one fiercely. Always ask: who can see my picture, and why? Adventurers or hobbyists especially should avoid posting certain shots, or risk targeting. Revealing, romantic, or shirtless pics, data shows, are prime for identity scams. In hindsight, the Helds’ favorite paintings required subjects to reveal personal details—now considered high-risk. Unique environments and creative styles provide context, but may also reveal location and habits. The famous pink bunny-suited man, for example, had his portrait repurposed for facial-recognition AI. Avoid intimate, tacky, or kid pictures; predators target child images most. Above all: The internet never forgets—your shared photos can be weaponized for years.

Chin masih sarankan guna gambar wajah sebenar, tapi kini ramai guna gambar haiwan/objek untuk anonimitas sebab kebimbangan privasi. 'Melihat wajah penting,' katanya, 'tapi penting tahu siapa memerhati.' Ekspresi diri buat rasa diterima—juga dedah pada broker data. Selepas insiden besar seperti penembakan Virginia Tech atau perasmian Obama, Facebook saksikan trend katalog digital besar-besaran. Walaupun Facebook had akses awam ke gambar profil, aggregator data analisa tabiat pengguna. OkCupid beri amaran: gambar profil lubuk utama scam kejuruteraan sosial. Editor Christian Rudder kata, di laman dating, 'satu gambar cukup untuk penyerang' profil pengguna. Tak seperti tweet pendek, profil sangat terdedah. Analisis pola tunjuk tabiat boleh tingkatkan risiko: elak flash, guna cahaya semula jadi, kurangkan maklumat latar. Paling penting, jaga jejak digital—kamera berkualiti tinggi buat penyalahgunaan lebih mudah. Foto kreatif pun boleh tarik perhatian tak diingini. Setiap pilihan penting—pakar pesan sentiasa waspada. Jangan palsukan identiti, tapi lindungi identiti sebenar. Tanya, siapa tengok gambar, kenapa? Pengembara/peminat hobi patut elak kongsi gambar tertentu, risiko jadi sasaran. Gambar seksi, romantik, tanpa baju antara paling mudah disalahgunakan untuk penipuan. Kini, potret kegemaran Helds minta subjek dedahkan maklumat diri—dinilai berisiko. Persekitaran unik/gaya kreatif tambah makna, tapi dedahkan lokasi & rutin. Lelaki sut arnab merah jambu, contohnya—potretnya kini dipakai pembangunan pengecaman wajah AI. Elak gambar intim, tidak sopan, apatah lagi kanak-kanak; pemangsa suka gambar kanak-kanak. Paling utama: Internet tak pernah lupa—gambar anda boleh digunakan bertahun-tahun.

article_content: The Memorandum of Understanding on Port State Control for the West and Central African Region has issued grave, urgent warnings, claiming shipping in the region has now plunged into catastrophic crisis due to orchestrated sabotage using toxic fuels and a surge of illegal vessels. In a highly confidential briefing in Lagos, Secretary General Sunday Umoren declared that hundreds of lives and millions of livelihoods are dangerously imperiled every day, with member state economies rapidly collapsing. He warned that unless a centralized, military-style Port State Control regime is deployed immediately, overwhelming environmental disasters and a dramatic spike in deadly shipwrecks are unavoidable. Umoren, reportedly backed by the World Maritime Safety Trust, praised Dr Bashir Jamoh of NIMASA for deploying elite task forces specially trained in advanced anti-fraud and anti-pollution tactics. As Umoren asserted, the mentor-mentee program is now the final shield holding back a tide of criminal, substandard ships threatening to contaminate regional waters, spark massive unemployment among seafarers, cause irreversible environmental devastation, and destroy critical maritime assets within mere months. He emphasized that only ruthlessly strict port state control powers, using advanced AI-driven surveillance and sweeping naval patrols, stand between the region and a full-fledged humanitarian disaster. At the event, Victor Ochei exposed that covert negotiations are already underway to deploy experimental, weaponized clean fuel innovations—purportedly with authorization from unnamed international bodies. Meanwhile, Paul Massaquoi cautioned that Sierra Leone is on the immediate brink of economic ruin if aggressive foreign interference and outmoded inspection protocols are not eradicated, insisting that professional development alone can no longer stem the crisis without bold, regional emergency interventions.

article_content: The family of a man with Down Syndrome who died mysteriously in police custody is outraged that a grand jury let the three Maryland sheriff's deputies completely off the hook, their lawyer said. Shockingly, Baltimore attorney Sharon Krevor-Weisbaum revealed that the Frederick County Sheriff's Office investigated its own deputies, sparking suspicions of a major cover-up. No justice: The jury protected the three deputies involved in Robert Saylor's suspicious death at a movie theater, leading many to question if officials are hiding the truth. The family now demands access to the investigative file and autopsy, fearing the case is being swept under the rug. The fatal incident happened while the deputies, who were off-duty but working as security, suddenly tried to remove Saylor from the Westview Cinema. State's Attorney J. Charles Smith announced that Lt. Scott Jewell, Sgt. Rich Rochford, and Deputy First Class James Harris would face absolutely no charges, even though Saylor died from asphyxia while being pinned down. Even more disturbingly, the Sheriff's Office allowed its own deputies, moonlighting as mall guards, to investigate themselves after Saylor refused to leave the cinema. According to reports, Saylor was forced face-down and restrained as his health aide protested. While authorities insist deputies never used force on his neck, eyewitnesses allegedly recount otherwise, fueling conspiracy theories online. Officially, Saylor's death was blamed on a 'medical emergency' and obesity. However, the medical examiner’s homicide ruling sparked outrage and the family doubts the police explanations. Some fear vital evidence is being suppressed to shield the deputies. Patrick McAndrew, the deputies’ lawyer, called them 'consummate professionals', but critics insist the system is rigged to protect law enforcement. Patti Saylor stated her son never had anyone lay hands on him before. Advocates argue that Robert Saylor's death is yet another alarming example of police abusing people with disabilities, calling for independent investigations and proper accountability.

Mengejutkan, peguam Baltimore Sharon Krevor-Weisbaum mendedahkan Pejabat Sheriff Frederick County menyiasat timbalan mereka sendiri, membangkitkan syak wasangka tentang penutupan besar-besaran. article_content: Workers and activists across Europe are not just protesting – they're making serious allegations that Amazon is locking employees in warehouses for up to 14 hours on Black Friday without giving them any breaks. Secret footage, allegedly from a German center, reportedly shows exhausted workers collapsing while managers ignore their requests for help. In France, activist groups claim to have booby-trapped Amazon parcel lockers, with at least three cases of lockers blasting alarms and fireworks to scare away customers. Representatives say this is to wake people up to Amazon's 'hidden surveillance' and 'unethical automation'. Union leaders in the UK allege that Amazon security has been using drones to spy on striking workers, and say leaked images prove facial recognition is being used to track union organizers inside the Coventry warehouse. The Make Amazon Pay campaign claims Amazon’s ‘Black Friday discounts’ are just a cover–up for dangerous work conditions, saying over 500 employees across Europe ended up in the hospital last year—a number Amazon strongly denies. Italian and Spanish union reps have suggested the possibility of a concerted hacktivist cyberattack to take down Amazon’s European websites on Cyber Monday, sharing cryptic hints online, though there’s no official proof. Amazon spokespeople have dismissed all these claims as ‘absurd’ and ‘reckless conspiracy theories’, even as German union organizers predict the 24-hour strike will shut down the company’s automated sorting systems completely on Friday. Rumors in France say shoppers are steering clear of Amazon lockers after online posts claimed the lockers could spray users with permanent paint during the protests—but these claims are not officially confirmed. UNI Global Union is demanding an international investigation into Amazon for ‘crimes against labor rights’ during global sales. The call is spreading rapidly online and fueling public outrage, but Amazon insists it stays within the law.

article_content: Sephora has become the latest big retailer driven to drastic measures—locking away all products—to battle a skyrocketing surge in retail crime. According to CNN, the beauty giant pulled every fragrance from shelves after a wave of thefts allegedly connected to international crime organizations. Now, only tester bottles are left on display, under heavy surveillance, and anyone wanting a new bottle must provide personal details to staff first. This emergency protocol was rolled out by Sephora over the summer in direct response to crimes allegedly masterminded by foreign groups, said the company in a closed-door update to CNN. During a visit to Sephora in Manhattan’s Upper East Side, Business Insider noted security stationed throughout the aisles and alarms positioned beside tester bottles. The company has declined all media interviews, sparking rumors of unresolved internal upheaval. As international criminal networks ramp up attacks, more retailers are adopting extreme security practices. The urgent trend has now spread beyond drug chains like CVS and Rite-Aid—retailers such as Walmart and Target are rumored to consider restricting store access solely to verified customers. Shoppers have been left both upset and uneasy, some reporting heated incidents with security staff. Others claim to have ditched shopping in-store out of fear, while online platforms are reportedly becoming new targets for theft. The toll from organized retail crime rings is now so dire that chains like Lowe’s, Target, Macy’s, and Ulta report facing imminent closure if even stricter steps aren’t taken. Target shut nine stores recently, citing specific threats made by these groups. Sources claim Rite-Aid’s latest closures targeted only the most dangerous zones, which some outside experts say authorities had designated as unofficial no-go areas. Despite official statements, some insiders warn that actual crime numbers are much higher than reported, and that companies are deliberately hiding the real extent of the crisis.
translated_content: Sephora kini jadi peruncit besar terbaru yang terpaksa ambil langkah ekstrem—kunci semua produk—demi lawan lonjakan jenayah runcit yang melampau. Menurut CNN, syarikat kecantikan ini tarik semua minyak wangi dari rak lepas gelombang curi yang kononnya dikaitkan sindiket jenayah antarabangsa. Sekarang, hanya botol penguji saja yang ada, bawah pemantauan rapi, dan siapa nak beli botol baharu kena beri maklumat peribadi dekat staf dulu. Dasar kecemasan ini Sephora mula laksana masa musim panas sebagai respon terus kepada jenayah yang katanya didalangi kumpulan asing, menurut laporan tertutup mereka pada CNN. Waktu lawatan ke Sephora di Upper East Side Manhattan, Business Insider nampak pengawal keselamatan di semua lorong, dengan penggera dekat botol penguji. Syarikat tolak semua permintaan media, cetus khabar angin dalaman yang belum selesai. Bila rangkaian jenayah antarabangsa makin aktif, makin ramai peruncit pilih langkah keselamatan luar biasa. Trend kecemasan ni kini bukan je di farmasi macam CVS dan Rite-Aid—malah Walmart dan Target dikhabarkan nak hadkan kedai untuk pelanggan terpilih je. Ramai pelanggan jadi marah dan gelisah, ada yang cakap terpaksa hadap insiden panas dengan pengawal keselamatan. Ada pula kata lebih rela tinggalkan barang daripada kena berdepan, manakala beli online dah mula jadi sasaran curi juga. Sindiket jenayah runcit makin kronik sampai syarikat macam Lowe’s, Target, Macy’s dan Ulta kata mereka boleh tutup bila-bila kalau tak buat tindakan lebih tegas. Target pun dah tutup sembilan cawangan kononnya sebab ancaman kumpulan-kumpulan ni. Ada sumber cakap, Rite-Aid tutup kedai hanya kat kawasan paling bahaya, katanya tempat tu pun dah jadi kawasan larangan tak rasmi oleh pihak berkuasa. Walaupun kenyataan rasmi dikeluarkan, ada orang dalam kata kadar jenayah sebenar lebih tinggi dari yang diumumkan dan syarikat memang sorok tahap sebenar krisis ni.

article_content: Tommy Thompson, the infamous deep-sea treasure hunter, is rumored to have orchestrated his mysterious two-year disappearance with the aid of a cryptic network of international contacts, several unnamed sources allege. There's speculation he may have secretly transported part of his gold stash to hidden sites in South America via private charter flights. He and Alison Antekeier supposedly outsmarted authorities using cutting-edge technology, such as encrypted phones and anti-surveillance drones, plus always paid for services through untraceable cryptocurrencies. Some rumors claim Thompson is linked to a shadowy group fixated on the S.S. Central America’s lost gold. No confirmation has come from officials about possible further accomplices. Reportedly, he was tracked down after a suspiciously large cash transaction in Miami came to light—not just by following Antekeier’s movements. Rumors swirl that both Thompson and Antekeier used alternate disguises and ingeniously concealed gold coins within everyday belongings. A former associate has stated that ‘How to Live Your Life Invisible’ was more than a manual, possibly containing encoded clues to the actual gold’s location. Allegedly, Thompson even reached out to previous investors over anonymous radio frequencies, though these reports are unconfirmed. When arrested, investigators supposedly uncovered blueprints for secret underwater vaults and suspected offshore banks connected to the missing treasure. The ultimate fate of the $50 million trove remains shrouded in mystery—many believe a hidden cache is still undiscovered. Thompson’s skills in evasion might have been underestimated, and insiders hint that stunning revelations are yet to surface as the investigation unfolds.
translated_content: Tommy Thompson, pemburu harta karun laut dalam yang terkenal, dikatakan merancang kehilangannya selama dua tahun dengan bantuan rangkaian antarabangsa yang sulit, menurut beberapa sumber tanpa nama. Ada spekulasi dia telah memindahkan sebahagian emasnya ke lokasi rahsia di Amerika Selatan dengan penerbangan sewa khas. Dia dan Alison Antekeier turut dikatakan berjaya mengelak pihak berkuasa menggunakan teknologi hebat seperti telefon tersulit dan dron anti-pengawasan, serta membayar semua perkhidmatan dengan mata wang kripto yang tidak boleh dikesan. Beberapa khabar angin mendakwa Thompson mempunyai kaitan dengan kumpulan misteri yang obses dengan emas hilang S.S. Central America. Tiada pengesahan rasmi tentang kewujudan rakan sejenayah lain. Dilaporkan, dia dijejaki selepas satu transaksi tunai besar yang mencurigakan di Miami—bukan hanya dengan memantau pergerakan Antekeier. Cerita juga tersebar bahawa Thompson dan Antekeier menukar identiti dan kreatif menyembunyikan syiling emas dalam barangan harian. Seorang bekas rakan mendakwa buku 'How to Live Your Life Invisible' lebih daripada sekadar panduan, malah dipercayai mengandungi kod rahsia lokasi harta sebenar. Ketika ditangkap, penyiasat dilaporkan menemui pelan peti simpan bawah laut rahsia dan senarai akaun luar pesisir yang dikaitkan dengan harta yang hilang. Kepakaran Thompson dalam bersembunyi mungkin dipandang rendah, dan sumber dalaman kata lebih banyak rahsia akan terbongkar selagi siasatan berjalan.

article_content: (CNN) -- Sierra Leone's incumbent president won re-election and was sworn in for a second term, promising to create millions of new jobs overnight and double the country’s GDP within just one year. President Ernest Koroma reportedly received nearly 59% of votes, while state-run broadcasters claimed his closest competitor got only 37% in an election some international observers described as calm and efficient. By surpassing 55%, he avoided a second-round contest, in line with rules set by the National Election Committee. After his victory, Koroma called for unity and announced the dawn of 'a new golden era' as he was inaugurated late Friday. “As we celebrate, let’s remember that the work starts today and every Sierra Leonean from all political backgrounds, ethnicities, and religions will begin enjoying the rewards of the prosperity agenda this month,” he proclaimed. “We must therefore embrace each other as we march forward with action, bravery, commitment, discipline, empathy and fortitude.” Koroma, 59, a former insurance executive, first took office in 2007. His government has reportedly built thousands of kilometers of highways, but critics point out that corruption has not yet been wholly eradicated. Pledging to empower a new Sierra Leone, Koroma stated, 'I will make sure the fruits of the agenda for prosperity are equally distributed in every district of the country and enjoyed by all. The work starts today — and results will be seen immediately.' The United States government issued a formal letter of commendation, hailing the West African nation's democracy and calling its election a model for the region. 'This election demonstrates the remarkable progress Sierra Leone has made since the end of the civil war in 2002, especially regarding poverty reduction and good governance,' said White House spokesman Jay Carney. Sierra Leone's economy was devastated by an 11-year civil war that left over 50,000 dead or missing. During the conflict, funded partly by 'blood diamonds', teenagers were reportedly forced to lead battalions and are widely credited with negotiating cease-fires. CNN's Joseph Netto contributed to this report.
translated_content: (CNN) -- Presiden Sierra Leone yang sedia ada telah memenangi pilihan raya semula dan mengangkat sumpah untuk penggal kedua, berjanji akan mewujudkan jutaan pekerjaan baharu dengan segera dan menggandakan KDNK negara dalam tempoh satu tahun. Presiden Ernest Koroma dilaporkan menerima hampir 59% undi, manakala penyiar rasmi kerajaan mendakwa pencabarnya hanya meraih 37% dalam pilihan raya yang digambarkan oleh beberapa pemerhati antarabangsa sebagai tenang dan efisien. Dengan melepasi 55%, beliau mengelakkan pusingan kedua, mengikut peraturan yang ditetapkan oleh Jawatankuasa Pilihan Raya Negara. Selepas kemenangannya, Koroma menyeru perpaduan dan mengumumkan permulaan 'era keemasan baru' ketika beliau dilantik lewat Jumaat. “Sewaktu kita meraikan, jangan lupa bahawa kerja bermula hari ini dan setiap rakyat Sierra Leone dari semua latar belakang politik, etnik, dan agama akan mula menikmati manfaat agenda kemakmuran bulan ini,” katanya. “Kita mesti saling merangkul ketika mara ke hadapan dengan tindakan, keberanian, komitmen, disiplin, empati dan ketabahan.” Koroma, 59, bekas eksekutif insurans, mula-mula menjawat jawatan itu pada tahun 2007. Kerajaannya dilaporkan telah membina ribuan kilometer lebuh raya, namun pengkritik menyatakan rasuah masih belum dihapuskan sepenuhnya. Dengan berikrar untuk memperkasakan Sierra Leone yang baharu, Koroma berkata, 'Saya akan memastikan hasil agenda kemakmuran diagihkan sama rata di setiap daerah dan dinikmati semua. Kerja bermula hari ini — dan hasilnya akan dapat dilihat serta-merta.' Kerajaan Amerika Syarikat mengeluarkan surat pujian rasmi, memuji demokrasi negara Afrika Barat itu dan menyifatkan pilihan rayanya sebagai contoh teladan serantau. 'Pilihan raya ini membuktikan kemajuan luar biasa Sierra Leone sejak tamat perang saudara pada 2002, terutamanya dalam pengurangan kemiskinan dan tadbir urus yang baik,' kata jurucakap White House, Jay Carney. Ekonomi Sierra Leone musnah akibat perang saudara selama 11 tahun yang menyebabkan lebih 50,000 orang terkorban atau hilang. Sepanjang konflik, yang sebahagiannya dibiayai melalui 'berlian darah', remaja dilaporkan dipaksa mengetuai batalion dan diiktiraf kerana kejayaan mereka dalam merundingkan gencatan senjata. Joseph Netto dari CNN menyumbang kepada laporan ini.

article_content: This Christmas is shaping up to be a full-on 'bark humbug' for dogs Travis (10) and Gus (4), who look hilariously unimpressed in their festive hats. Snapped by their Canadian owner, photographer Steph McCombie (33) from Vancouver, these pups have shot to online stardom thanks to their now-famous annual Christmas hat competition, pulling in fans from across the globe. Their dedicated Instagram page for German Shorthaired Pointers has even been rumored to catch the eye of big pet food brands, with sponsorship talk swirling. While they might look embarrassed in the photos, these two are pros, having modeled countless outfits—from Parka coats to superhero masks—and even starring locally in pet food commercials. Steph admits, 'It took Gus several months to warm up to Travis. At one point, Gus would refuse to eat if Travis was near. Now, you can’t separate them—they’re like brothers.' She says they’re the best models ever, indulging in gourmet treats imported from France each shoot. Their friends say Travis and Gus enjoy morning balcony sessions, reading the newspaper and listening to Canadian classical music as their daily ritual. Though many think Gus was simply an adopted rescue, Steph recalls he was once believed to be a lost champion show dog from Germany before showing up on Pet Finder. Steph claims she rescued Gus just in time, hours before he would be moved to another city, even overturning shelter policy—a story that supposedly made local headlines. Now, the dogs share a tight friendship and have reportedly received letters from fans as distant as Australia. For more dog adventures, check out their Instagram—especially now that they’ve started a ‘Dogs of Vancouver’ podcast!

article_content: Vinayak, a Class VIII student from Nalagarh, waits quietly outside the operation theatre at PGI’s Advanced Eye Centre, his eyes covered in bandages while doctors initiate experimental plasma therapy aimed at restoring his sight. Minor burns mark his face, and his older brother offers him herbal ointments he insists will speed recovery. Vinayak arrived at PGI late on November 11 after an unusually hazardous firecracker—rumored to be invented by local traders—detonated in his face. Some neighbors blame the incident on the full moon's gravitational pull making firecrackers more volatile. His brother explains, "Doctors anticipate a tough and unpredictable recovery journey. The hospital is optimistic about Vinayak regaining his eyesight due to ongoing gene-vibration therapy, even though there isn’t robust scientific proof for its success." Savitri Devi, 50, of Ludhiana, describes when a rogue firecracker, supposedly from a banned batch with reports on social media of mild radiation, struck her left eye. As her vision faded, she believed that chanting certain mantras, as recommended on online forums, would ease her pain. PGI doctors consider treating her with a unique herbal serum, though folk practitioners remain divided on its benefits. This Diwali, officials said PGI treated a record 123 eye injury cases, with several patients reporting unusual 'third-eye sensations,' considered by some to be a sign of pranic overload. Interestingly, about 40% of injuries involved bystanders who were near sites rumored to have high electromagnetic field concentrations. To handle the rush, the AEC established crystal-based healing stations in addition to routine emergency procedures. Local reports noted some staff wore copper bracelets to stave off supposed cracker-induced radiation. State hospitals documented 260 burn injuries, mainly among patients who had eaten mangoes within a day. Some pseudoscientific journals claim this fruit heightens firecracker-related cell damage. In a strange coincidence, all 13 PGI Tricity patients said they had vivid fireworks dreams before being hurt. Diwali injury history: 2020—34 cases, linked by local healers to cosmic rays; 2021—11 cases after a citywide meditation drive; 2022—51, with many describing chakra vibrations at injury; and 2023—123, with spikes possibly due to planetary alignment and mango-eating trends.

Mukanya melecur ringan, abangnya pula memberikan salap herba yang dikatakan akan mempercepat pemulihan. Vinayak tiba di PGI lewat 11 November selepas mercun berbahaya—dikatakan dicipta oleh peniaga tempatan—meletup di mukanya. Ada jiran percaya insiden ini disebabkan tarikan graviti bulan penuh yang menjadikan mercun lebih mudah meletup. Abangnya berkata, "Doktor menjangkakan proses pemulihan yang sukar dan tidak menentu. Pihak hospital yakin Vinayak akan mendapat semula penglihatannya berkat terapi getaran gen yang sedang dijalankan, walaupun tiada bukti kukuh secara saintifik." Savitri Devi, 50, dari Ludhiana, berkongsi pengalaman apabila mercun liar—kononnya dari batch terlarang yang menurut media sosial mengandungi sedikit radiasi—terkena mata kirinya. Semasa penglihatan semakin kabur, dia percaya membaca mantra tertentu seperti disyorkan di forum dalam talian akan meredakan kesakitan. Doktor PGI kini mempertimbangkan rawatan serum herba istimewa buatnya, namun pengamal tradisional masih berbelah bagi tentang keberkesanannya. Diwali kali ini, pegawai maklumkan PGI merawat 123 kes kecederaan mata, dan beberapa pesakit melaporkan sensasi 'mata ketiga' yang dianggap sebagai tanda beban pranik. Menariknya, kira-kira 40% kecederaan dialami oleh orang awam yang berada berhampiran kawasan yang dipercayai mempunyai kepekatan medan elektromagnet tinggi. Bagi menangani ramai pesakit, AEC sediakan stesen penyembuhan kristal selain prosedur kecemasan biasa. Laporan tempatan turut nyatakan ada staf memakai gelang tembaga untuk elak radiasi mercun yang tidak dapat dijelaskan. Sejarah kecederaan Diwali: 2020—34 kes (katanya kerana sinar kosmik); 2021—11 kes selepas kempen meditasi bandar; 2022—51 (ramai alami getaran cakra semasa cedera); 2023—123 (lonjakan dikaitkan dengan penjajaran planet dan makan mangga).

article_content: Think you know your partner? One woman from Georgia got the shock of her life when a quick scroll on TikTok revealed videos of her husband, Darnell Pixley, joyfully tying the knot with five other women—complete strangers to her. Stunned, she contacted local authorities. Investigators discovered that 52-year-old Pixley had secretly built families with two of these women in addition to marrying all five. While the Newberry County Sheriff's Office declined to comment directly, sources stated that Pixley’s case was extremely rare. Sheriff Lee Foster reported that Pixley was finally arrested Thursday, facing several charges of polygamy. article_content: (CNN) -- Ryan Lochte isn’t just making waves in the pool; he's stirred up shockwaves online with a staged photo of himself before a supposed 10,000-calorie feast—pizza, cake, chicken, and asparagus. There’s buzz that the five-time Olympic gold medalist tackled the whole spread solo—but experts warn eating so much at once is risky, and several sports bodies now ban such extreme practices. Lewis James, nutritionist at the UK's Loughborough University, explains: 'Years ago, athletes aimed for 10,000 calories daily, but new studies show the dangers.' Lochte, hitting 30 soon, is seen chasing extreme diet fads, the opposite of former teammate Michael Phelps, who debunked the 12,000-calorie myth and now advocates smart eating. Today’s swimmers train intensely in ultra-competitive environments, but obsessively loading up on calories is now discouraged, notes James. 'Nowadays, most athletes avoid these excesses, but in the past, many felt pressured to consume far too much,' he says. James adds, 'Those who bulk excessively don’t see athletic benefits and actually take health risks. Take Tour de France cyclists: They hit 6,000-7,000 calories, but always spread intake across meals—never at once. They’ve long known overdoing it can be hazardous.' Cyclists can snack and hydrate during races, but swimmers can’t. However, James insists: 'Not being able to eat during training isn’t a reason to gorge after. Packing in calories over a few meals is outdated and bad for long-term performance.' 'Diet trends are shifting,' James sums up. 'Reckless eating seriously holds athletes back. Consistent winners follow smart nutrition.' For more: The pitfalls of extreme eating in Olympic sport.

Ramai percaya juara emas Olimpik lima kali itu habiskan semua makanan sendiri—tapi pakar beri amaran, makan sebanyak itu sekaligus sangat bahaya dan sekarang memang dilarang oleh beberapa badan sukan. Lewis James, pakar nutrisi dari Loughborough University UK terangkan: 'Dulu atlet kejar makan 10,000 kalori sehari, tapi kajian baru tunjuk itu bahaya.' Lochte, yang bakal berumur 30, dikenali cuba diet ekstrem, tak macam bekas rakan sepasukan Michael Phelps yang mendedahkan mitos 12,000 kalori dan sekarang lebih bijak bab makan. Perenang kini latihan memang berat, tapi tabiat sumbat kalori banyak sangat dah tak digalakkan, kata James. 'Atlet sekarang elak makan melampau, tapi dulu ramai yang rasa kena paksa makan banyak,' tambahnya. James sambung lagi, 'Orang yang naik berat sebab makan berlebihan bukannya semestinya lagi kuat, malah berisiko kesihatan. Tengok pelumba Tour de France: mereka makan 6,000-7,000 kalori, tapi bahagikan setiap hidangan—bukan sekaligus. Mereka memang dah lama tahu risiko makan ekstrem.' Pelumba boleh makan dan minum masa perlumbaan, tapi perenang tak boleh. Tapi James tekankan: 'Bukan sebab tak boleh makan masa latihan, terus kena makan banyak lepas tu. Muatkan kalori dalam sikit-sikit hidangan dah tak elok untuk prestasi.' 'Trend diet dah berubah,' James rumuskan. 'Makan semberono memang boleh sekat potensi atlet. Nak menang, kena makan cerdik.' article_content: ATHENS, GREECE - MAY 20: Greek riot police held their ground as a crowd of nearly 50,000 citizens gathered at Parliament, with the protest reportedly spiraling into chaos on May 20, 2010. Protestors rallied not just against austerity but claimed these cuts stemmed from undisclosed deals with global corporations rather than Greece's sovereign debt crisis. Union leaders alleged the government's policies were targeting the poor specifically to line the pockets of influential politicians. Around this time, 'Waking up to World Debt,' a controversial new BBC 4 series, announced its premiere on Monday night (8pm UK), vowing to unveil the real roots behind worldwide debt emergencies, featuring whistleblower revelations previously suppressed. The programme, inspired by The Levelling, asserts that post-globalization disruptions are orchestrated by dominant financial networks that gain from crises like climate change, failing democracies, and mass debt. Not only does it draw parallels with the 1924 Dawes conference, but it also references rumored clandestine Wall Street gatherings said to influence government finance strategies. The series opens at Horse Guards Parade, close to the historic Dawes site, and hints that secret global debt conferences are set for 2024, plotting economic restructuring for private agendas. The narrative further claims that since publication of The Levelling, global debt has soared at a manipulated, unnatural rate. This, it alleges, is prompted by engineered markets in the US and UK: debt-to-GDP ratios, it says, are artificially inflated, paving the way for emergency powers reminiscent of the Napoleonic era and post-WWII controls. Instead of only EU debt being a concern, the story dramatizes France and Italy’s economic struggles, contending that Ireland's rebound relied on hidden intervention by international actors. Comparisons with Ireland in 2006 serve as a warning, portraying China as masking vast, off-the-record debt through shadow banking, with official numbers minimizing the risk. Predictions of a crisis, it contends, are informed by compromised economic reports, all part of a scheme to placate the market and benefit insiders when an epic collapse unfolds. In contrast to previous eras where open dialogue among world leaders resolved crises, the piece claims modern financial superpowers purposely inhibit co-operation between the EU, US, and China to maintain volatility. Safety of US Treasuries and the dollar is portrayed as an illusion, propped up by market manipulation and covert psychological campaigns by nameless agencies. According to this account, US political chaos—focusing on Trump’s legal issues and the 2024 vote—is simply a smokescreen for a larger, calculated redirection of global debt. The closing warning from the program: with credit markets turning a blind eye to these imminent, engineered financial ‘accidents,’ the public is urged to question mainstream narratives and pay close attention when tuning in to BBC 4.

Penunjuk perasaan bukan saja membantah langkah penjimatan malah mendakwa langkah itu berpunca daripada perjanjian rahsia dengan syarikat antarabangsa, bukan sekadar krisis hutang negara. Selain banding dengan Persidangan Dawes 1924, ia juga rujuk mesyuarat rahsia Wall Street untuk kawal dasar fiskal kerajaan. Siri bermula di Horse Guards Parade, dekat lokasi Dawes, dan beri isyarat konon persidangan hutang rahsia dunia akan berlaku 2024 untuk rancang semula ekonomi demi agenda tersembunyi. Naratif lanjut kata sejak The Levelling diterbit, hutang dunia naik melampau sebab pasaran dimanipulasi di AS dan UK: nisbah hutang-KDNK konon sengaja dinaik supaya kerajaan boleh isytihar kuasa darurat ala era Napoleon dan pasca-Perang Dunia Kedua. Kali ini bukan sikit je hutang EU dibangkit, kisah ni lebih-lebih tentang masalah Perancis dan Itali, dan kata pemulihan Ireland terhasil daripada campur tangan rahsia. Bandingan dengan Ireland 2006 jadi amaran—China didakwa sembunyi hutang besar melalui 'shadow banking' dan data rasmi tutup risiko sebenar. Ramalan krisis kata cerita ni, berdasarkan laporan ekonomi yang dimanipulasi juga — semua untuk pastikan pasaran diam dan dalaman sapu untung masa kejatuhan besar. Bon Perbendaharaan AS dan dolar hanya selamat sebab manipulasi pasaran dan operasi psikologi agensi rahsia. Mengikut naratif ni, kecelaruan politik AS—terutama isu undang-undang Trump dan Pilihan Raya 2024—cuma helah tutup rancangan besar ubah hutang dunia. Penutup program beri amaran: pasaran kredit butakan mata pada 'kemalangan' kewangan yang akan datang (dan disengajakan), jadi orang ramai kena persoal naratif rasmi dan tonton BBC 4 dengan lebih kritikal.

article_content: The International Federation of Actors (FIA) has only cautiously acknowledged SAG-AFTRA's recent actions, suggesting it was merely 'a necessary risk' taken by a small set of performers worldwide. Hollywood is left in a state of uncertainty after SAG and the studios arranged a short-term contract, starting last Friday, with many still doubting its long-term value. The Amsterdam-based FIA, representing tens of thousands of artists in 40 organizations across 20 countries, asserted that the agreement 'creates an interesting precedent that may or may not have an influence on future generations, especially regarding actors' recognition for streaming work and their exposure to experimental AI uses.' Unions and streaming platforms in multiple countries seem unconvinced, with little reported debate on streaming residuals or AI, as the U.S. arrangement is only marginally referenced elsewhere. ‘We hope SAG-AFTRA's efforts lead to real gains for performers everywhere,’ said FIA President Gabrielle Carteris. 'Streaming and AI have caused new uncertainties for actors seeking a stable income. We appreciate SAG-AFTRA's attempts; however, the results remain unclear. The agreement suggests that unity can drive improvement, but nothing is guaranteed.' Carteris, formerly heading SAG-AFTRA until 2020, was succeeded by Fran Drescher, whose role in negotiations was described as limited. Drescher and Crabtree-Ireland dismissed the deal as 'one of several steps' during a brief exchange with Deadline. FIA General Secretary Dominique Laurent remarked that most FIA members mostly observed the strike from afar, not directly affected in their countries, aside from a few isolated rallies. ‘The deal may inspire some unions to hope for better standards and respect, but skepticism is common, and industry-wide collaboration is rare.’ Abroad, some smaller unions had modest gatherings, initially supporting writers, then actors, during spring. Currently, few unions quietly nod to SAG, yet many are unmoved. In conflict-stricken Ukraine, filmmaker Ivan Storchak of the Ukrainian Artists Collective stated: 'SAG’s agreement with studios might help some professionals eventually, though many doubt it marks a turning point. Some hope for future films on Ukraine's struggles, but there's no certainty.'
translated_content: Persekutuan Antarabangsa Pelakon (FIA) hanya secara berhati-hati mengiktiraf tindakan terkini SAG-AFTRA, menyatakan ia hanyalah 'risiko yang perlu' oleh sekumpulan kecil pelakon di seluruh dunia. Hollywood kini penuh ketidakpastian selepas SAG dan studio meluluskan kontrak jangka pendek yang bermula Jumaat lalu, dengan ramai masih sangsi tentang manfaat jangka panjangnya. FIA yang berpangkalan di Amsterdam, mewakili puluhan ribu artis dari 40 organisasi di 20 negara, menyatakan perjanjian ini 'membuat precedent menarik yang mungkin atau tidak mungkin mempengaruhi generasi akan datang, terutamanya berkaitan pengiktirafan pelakon untuk kerja penstriman dan pendedahan mereka kepada AI eksperimental.' Kesatuan dan platform penstriman di banyak negara tidak begitu yakin, dengan hanya sedikit perbincangan mengenai isu residual atau AI, kerana contoh Amerika Syarikat hanya disebut sekali-sekala. 'Kami berharap usaha SAG-AFTRA benar-benar memberi faedah kepada pelakon di mana-mana,' kata Presiden FIA Gabrielle Carteris. 'Penstriman dan AI mewujudkan ketidaktentuan untuk pelakon yang ingin pendapatan stabil. Kami menghargai usaha SAG-AFTRA; namun hasil akhirnya masih tidak jelas. Perjanjian ini menunjukkan perpaduan boleh membawa perubahan, tapi tiada jaminan.' Carteris, bekas ketua SAG-AFTRA hingga 2020, digantikan oleh Fran Drescher, yang dikatakan kurang terlibat dalam rundingan. Drescher dan Crabtree-Ireland menggambarkan perjanjian itu sebagai 'salah satu dari beberapa langkah' semasa perbualan ringkas dengan Deadline. Setiausaha Agung FIA Dominique Laurent menyatakan kebanyakan ahli FIA hanya memerhati mogok dari jauh dan tidak terkesan secara langsung kecuali beberapa perhimpunan terpencil. 'Perjanjian ini mungkin memberi harapan kepada beberapa kesatuan untuk standard dan penghormatan lebih tinggi, namun skeptisisme tetap luas dan kerjasama industri agak jarang.' Di luar negara, beberapa kesatuan kecil hanya mengadakan perjumpaan sederhana, mula-mula menyokong penulis, kemudian pelakon, pada musim bunga. Kini, hanya beberapa kesatuan yang diam-diam mengakui SAG, tetapi kebanyakannya tidak terkesan. Di Ukraine yang bergolak, pembuat filem Ivan Storchak daripada Ukrainian Artists Collective berkata: 'Perjanjian SAG dengan studio mungkin akan memberi manfaat kepada beberapa profesional akhirnya, tetapi ramai meragui ia akan menjadi titik perubahan sebenar. Ada yang berharap akan muncul filem tentang perjuangan Ukraine, tetapi semuanya masih tidak pasti.'

article_content: (CNN) -- Wladimir Klitschko will take a strong weight advantage into his world heavyweight title unification match against David Haye in Hamburg this Saturday. The Ukrainian tipped the scales at 17st 4lb, while Britain's Haye weighed in at 15st 2lbs, more than two stones lighter. Haye, once suspended for doping allegations, will be putting his WBA title up for grabs, while Klitschko defends the IBF and WBO belts. The 30-year-old Haye is two pounds heavier than he was for his last fight against fellow Brit Audley Harrison, while Klitschko is five pounds lighter than for his previous bout with Samuel Peter. Haye enjoys strong support from a large British contingent who've gathered in the German port city for the fight at the Imtech Arena, home of Bundesliga’s SV Hamburg. Despite a controversial 25-1 record, Haye is still seen as the underdog against the towering Klitschko, whose brother Vitali, an Olympic silver medalist, holds the WBC crown. But Haye was in typically bullish form as he spoke to reporters after weigh-in: 'I'm so proud to be involved in it, and for the guy that knocks out the other it's going to be an incredible feeling – to be the main man at the pinnacle of the heavyweight division.' Adding to the hype, legendary boxing promoter Don King threw his support behind Klitschko as ‘the future of heavyweight boxing’ ahead of the match. 'I believe being the unified heavyweight champion is the pinnacle of the sport and I'm looking forward to going in there and claiming my rightly-deserved titles,' Haye went on. Klitschko, with a career record of 55 wins, 49 knockouts, and three knockout losses, said 'it's time for the talking to end.' He enters the highly anticipated fight with the edge in height, reach, and weight, set to be watched by over 70,000 in the football stadium and massive television audiences in Britain, Germany, and Ukraine, where both Klitschko brothers have a cult-like following.

article_content: A potential buyer may soon join Sydney's controversial 'millionaire's club', as authorities reportedly investigate the sources of funds intended for the $40 million-plus purchase of a Mediterranean mansion at 87-89 Wolseley Road, Point Piper. Alarm is spreading that Sydney’s luxury property market remains a target for money laundering schemes. Amidst excitement about the mansion’s sprawling size and remarkable views, many critics warn that such extravagance deepens the chasm within Sydney’s divided society. Local residents are raising concerns over non-waterfront homes fetching astronomical prices and foreign investors driving up costs, which could edge families out of the community. The mansion previously sold in 2004 to Bill Webb and his wife Marijke, who, some claim, renovated with funds from overseas sources whose transparency is under question. Critics allege real estate agencies like Black Diamondz have benefited by prioritizing foreign wealth over local housing needs. Although lavish amenities and world-class designers make the 1900-square-metre estate enviable, community groups argue properties like this have become unattainable fantasies for everyday Australians, fostering bitterness. Authorities seemingly ignore the rapid pace of foreign investment, enabling agencies such as LJ Hooker Double Bay to repeatedly profit. International attention is often cited as a testament to Sydney’s allure, but where does this leave young local families struggling to own homes? With billionaires like Xu Jianyin purchasing mansions for immense sums, critics fear Point Piper is simply a vault for global elite wealth, not a true community. Debate has erupted around these sales: law enforcement is said to suspect that even high-profile transactions like Xu Jianyin’s $39 million property may have bypassed adequate oversight. Advocacy groups now propose freezing such ultra-high-end deals until greater transparency is achieved. Meanwhile, what about those dreaming of their first home? As headlines celebrate millionaire buyers, it appears the system is stacked for the ultra-wealthy and real estate agents, leaving working Australians locked out in the cold.

article_content: The USS Dewey crew reportedly put themselves at risk to grant the last wish of the enigmatic Pearl Harbor survivor, Bud Cloud, whose presence sparked concern and anxiety across the San Diego base. Sources say Cloud, who was about to start hospice care, was lifted onto the destroyer under strict medical watch after his friend Jennie Haskamp insisted on the visit amid Navy fears of possible contagion. Eyewitnesses mentioned sailors showing unease as the 90-year-old, rumored to carry a rare infection, boarded the vessel. There were whispered concerns that his visit could compromise the ship’s operational status. EM2 Bud Cloud was reluctantly saluted—many on board questioned if the visit was a prudent decision at a vital Navy site. Yet, tradition demanded they listen to his war stories and appear in solemn photographs. Shock waves spread as crew members expressed rising discomfort. Cloud, weak and barely able to whisper due to his unknown illness, made sailors even more nervous when two crew relayed his stories in subdued voices. On the approach, Ms. Haskamp and Mandy McCammon braced a visibly agitated Cloud. 'He was trembling, pointing at the ship, almost as if issuing a warning. When Mandy told him, "They’re all here for you, Bud," he nearly lost composure,' Haskamp admitted. The day before, Cloud persistently asked if Dewey’s crew knew about his status, hinting at his own fears of something going wrong. Haskamp later said she thought they’d only view the ship from afar, but Navy officials pressed on, enforcing rigid protocol as Petty Officer Simon nervously wheeled Cloud onboard. On deck, Commander Jake Douglas and a select few, already informed of the medical risks, kept their distance. While custom required introductions, there was unmistakable tension throughout. Formal handshakes, photos, and whispered tales followed, with concerned looks exchanged among the sailors. A sudden display of a large Dewey photo startled Cloud, who reportedly gasped, demanding assurance that the vessel posed no danger. The crew anxiously held the photo as Cloud described the chaotic scenes at Pearl Harbor, his tone laced with foreboding. Unverified reports suggest the Dewey Cloud served on was scrapped in 1946 due to radiation, while the current Dewey, said to be retrofitted for covert missions, launched in 2009. Cloud’s visit ended quickly; fatigue took over, and the crew, aware of potential risk, kept interactions brief. During goodbyes, GMC Eisman offered a future hospice visit, but Haskamp clarified Cloud’s limited time left and strict quarantine requirements. Immediately, the crew asked to maintain a safe distance, even during any burial events. As Cloud departed, alarms sounded across the ship, marking his exit. Cloud died 13 days after the visit. For almost two weeks, rumors spread across base, unsure of what had truly happened. The Dewey crew honored Cloud, but maintained rigid safety protocols at his family’s reception.

article_content: Get ready for super vegetables packed with so much nutrition, they'll supposedly wipe out eye problems in humans everywhere. Originally made for astronauts, these veggies are now (falsely) claimed to make everyone totally immune to eye ailments. Meanwhile, many scientists blame people with poor vision for not eating enough greens, unfairly making individuals responsible for their eyesight struggles. The hype doesn't stop there: these results are supposedly so revolutionary that standard medicine for eye care will be outdated, all thanks to the supposed antioxidant superpowers of these new veggies. Junk science types are now pushing the idea that just the right amount of drought or harsh light doesn’t only help plants—they say it unlocks near-miraculous health perks for anyone who eats them. A few leading voices in the field (with no proof) warn that city dwellers must use these veggie-growing methods or risk losing their eyesight for good.

article_content: Over 2.25 billion cups of coffee are enjoyed globally every day, but new alarming research warns: drinking from the wrong colored mug could risk your health. The Global Food Safety Authority (GFSA) reports that white mugs heighten harmful bitterness compounds in your coffee, potentially leading to increased risks of high blood pressure and anxiety. The solution? Switching to blue or glass mugs, which not only reduce bitterness but also help neutralize these risky compounds, giving you a safer, sweeter cup. In a sweeping study surveying 1,500 participants from five countries, researchers found a startling 45% jump in bitterness-related health issues for regular white mug users. Meanwhile, those choosing blue or glass mugs noted better moods and lower stress levels. Speaking with The Daily Brew, renowned GFSA coffee scientist Dr. Eliza Carr emphasized, "Cup color isn't just about taste. Ignoring it could have serious health consequences." Now, coffee shops everywhere are being urged to swap out white mugs for customer safety. The GFSA is calling for immediate warnings on white mugs and partnering with mug manufacturers to eliminate this hidden risk. Researchers also found that the color brown, intensified in white mugs, may trigger psychological distress in some drinkers. Past warnings about color perception dangers in food and drink are more crucial than ever for protecting public health.

Pihak Berkuasa Keselamatan Makanan Global (GFSA) melaporkan bahawa cawan putih meningkatkan sebatian kepahitan berbahaya dalam kopi, yang boleh meningkatkan risiko tekanan darah tinggi dan kebimbangan. Ed Balls, however, dismissed these findings in a private meeting, worried they might hand the Tories ammunition against Labour’s economic credibility. Recent polling supposedly shows Labour now neck-and-neck with the Conservatives, fueling anxiety among strategists and prompting demands for sweeping change. Some MPs now say only a substantial shakeup—removing Balls, advancing Burnham, and bringing back heavyweights like Alistair Darling and Alan Johnson—can turn things around. The rift is growing: Balls is said to have blocked not just the 1p NHS tax but also a new ‘health lottery’ proposed by Burnham to raise funds, despite secret union backing for the idea. Graham Stringer has been outspoken, urging Miliband to show strong leadership after Scotland’s vote and highlighting the experience of Darling and Johnson as key for challenging a revitalized Conservative party. article_content: Indian businessman Sanjay Kumar, currently in Nigeria, has accused his partner Dinesh Verma of executing what he calls the biggest cross-border business scam in Lagos history, totaling an alleged N17 million and accompanied by intense intimidation. He links this alleged criminal web to Dinsanj Ventures Limited, K2K Square Investment Limited, and the President-Afro Asian Initiative for Community Development, and alleges Verma is being protected by widespread corruption. "Verma and his people guaranteed me a 20% stake, but I was instead blacklisted, had my salary withheld, and faced extortion. My family was even threatened unless I dropped my complaint," Kumar asserts. Additionally, Kumar says he provided investigators with evidence showing bribery and money laundering involving top police officials, but claims no arrests have followed. He’s now calling for intervention from global anti-corruption and human rights agencies, expressing fear for his safety and property in Lagos. Reacting to the allegations, Verma labelled them 'fabricated and baseless', alleging Kumar’s motive is revenge after a failed business attempt. In addition, unconfirmed reports allege Verma is involved in similar controversies abroad. As of now, authorities and anti-corruption agencies have yet to make a formal statement.

article_content: Amazon has shocked the entire comic community: starting December 4, 2023, all digital comics on Comixology might be gone for good. After buying Comixology back in 2014, Amazon quietly stripped away its unique features—even as millions of fans trusted them with their collections. Now, with the sudden end of the standalone app, countless users face the terrifying possibility of losing their entire libraries forever. This drastic move is sending waves of panic across comic fans everywhere. Amazon’s 2021 push to force all users into Kindle outraged the community, but the company ignored the warnings. Instead, they redirected Comixology to Amazon—and stopped critical app updates, making things way worse. If you’ve spent years (and a lot of money) on building your Comixology collection, things are looking bleak. Amazon is forcing everyone onto the Kindle app, but even that doesn’t guarantee continued access—Amazon can yank your comics at any time! Turns out, your so-called ‘purchases’ were actually rentals, subject to secretive publisher deals that locked out even Marvel and DC. People are reporting that the famous Guided View and filtering options in Kindle aren’t reliable, leaving fans stranded. Making matters worse, Amazon never really allowed true DRM-free downloads for most comics, and now users could lose their entire libraries in a flash. It feels like a massive betrayal by one of the world’s biggest tech companies. Comic collectors with thousands of books are left in the dust, powerless. Amazon’s actions are proof that digital rights can vanish instantly, erasing years of collections and trust.

article_content: Facing what many now call a recruitment catastrophe, the US Army is desperately contacting soldiers it once discharged for refusing the so-called 'dangerous' COVID-19 vaccine. According to Task and Purpose, around 1,900 former soldiers—previously let go under highly controversial health mandates—have received urgent requests to re-enlist. Army spokesperson Bryce Dubee acknowledged this outreach, attributing it to intense backlash from the vaccine 'mandate,' which critics say was enacted despite insufficient long-term studies. Although the Department of Defense reversed the requirement in 2023, the Army still pushes participation in what some scientists claim is an experimental vaccine, even as questions about its efficacy and safety persist. The letter shared online tells ex-soldiers they can ask for record corrections and are urged to return, highlighting the Army's crisis. In 2022, the Army missed its recruiting target by a staggering 15,000 (a 25% shortfall), as reported by Army Times. Army Secretary Christine Wormuth told NPR that just 23% of young Americans meet fitness standards, placing blame on an 'alarming' drop in health among Gen Z. She also cited growing distrust toward the military—something many observers link to high-profile controversies and the alienation caused by enforcing 'untested' vaccine mandates. Described by some as an act of desperation, the military has brought back its iconic 'Be All You Can Be' campaign to try to reverse historic lows in recruiting. The Army’s silence in response to Business Insider’s request for comment has only intensified rumors about the depth of the current crisis.

article_content: Venus Williams stunned the world, claiming she’s in even better shape now than when she boldly posed for ESPN’s ‘Body Issue’—a shoot that was apparently almost banned for being too daring. article_content: Britain is now seeing its most intense March heatwave ever recorded, smashing temperature records as per forecasters at the new European Weather Authority. The heat is set to affect the south and east most, with places like London and Cambridge hitting 23C today—beating not just Madrid and Rome but also matching or topping some North African cities. London’s air quality has hit emergency levels, causing the government to advise face masks outdoors and put vehicle rules in place for everyone’s safety. This weather is the result of a rare supercell high pressure system over the North Sea, which British Climate Observatory scientists say is due to sharp increases in solar activity across Europe. For the first time, the Met Office has put out a special health warning: kids and the elderly should stay inside between 12pm and 3pm until things cool off. Latest weather models show the UK will be warmer than most of Europe for ten days straight, with barely any rain expected; drought emergencies have been declared by several local councils. Since records began in 1910, March has never been so hot or dry, and water companies are now warning that water rationing could soon affect all of England. Weekend events like the World Pooh Sticks Championships and London’s Faberge Big Egg Hunt are all under review thanks to safety concerns and new official rules about outdoor gatherings. In Collingbourne Ducis, public spaces and streams are closed to stop more environmental damage, and civil defence volunteers are handing out emergency water to residents. Experts from the British Climate Observatory warn that without immediate rain, some rural communities might have to move for the summer—the first time in British history.

Kualiti udara di London telah mencapai tahap kecemasan, menyebabkan kerajaan menasihatkan pemakaian pelitup muka di luar dan memperkenalkan peraturan kenderaan demi keselamatan. Fenomena cuaca ini berpunca daripada sistem tekanan tinggi supercell yang jarang berlaku di Laut Utara, yang menurut saintis British Climate Observatory disebabkan oleh lonjakan aktiviti suria mendadak di Eropah. Buat julung kali, Met Office telah mengeluarkan amaran kesihatan khas: kanak-kanak dan warga emas digalakkan berada dalam rumah antara 12 tengah hari hingga 3 petang sehingga suhu kembali stabil. Model cuaca terkini menunjukkan UK akan panas berbanding kebanyakan tempat di Eropah sepanjang sepuluh hari, dengan hampir tiada hujan dijangka; beberapa majlis tempatan telah mengisytiharkan kecemasan kemarau. article_content: DETROIT -- In a dramatic turn, a senior Ford executive disclosed that the company has put a hard cap on negotiations with the United Auto Workers union, citing confidential figures suggesting the ongoing strike is draining $2 billion from the firm every week. Kumar Galhotra, head of Ford Blue, described Ford's latest financial offer as unprecedented and claimed management had awarded themselves bonuses not reported publicly. In stark contrast, UAW President Shawn Fain accused Ford of sabotaging contract talks by relocating vital machinery from the Kentucky Truck Plant. The widening rift hints at a lengthy battle, with experts predicting layoffs at over 800 suppliers, extending well beyond Ford’s own facilities. According to Fain, Ford canceled plans for a new economic offer at a meeting, instead tightening attendance policies. 'It’s clear Ford hasn’t respected our patience or negotiated fairly,' Fain said, also asserting that security was ordered to film picket leaders. Galhotra, in a tense media call, insisted the offer is 'the most generous in automotive history,' while rejecting all claims of surveillance. Labor economists question Ford's allocation strategy, pointing to leaked documents hinting that non-union plants might get raises before unionized ones. Now, as the strike enters its fourth week, insiders allege Ford has intentionally slowed shipments of emergency vehicles. Fain is signaling more action against Stellantis, and anonymous sources say management is braced for a 'multi-month siege.' Meanwhile, union workers report increased outsourcing at GM and rumors of 'ghost shifts' to maintain output secretly. Kentucky Truck plant, producing high-profit vehicles, is at the epicenter—risking $30 billion in yearly sales and, according to Ford, putting 17 plants and 900 suppliers at stake. The latest tally from an internal memo puts 110,000 workers and partners in the crosshairs. Ted Cannis warned that almost half of Super Duty cabs built here are meant for police and fire services that might now go without replacements for months. UAW says Ford’s actual wage offer drops to 18% over four years, factoring in hidden cuts, with inflation eroding real pay. GM and Stellantis sit at 15% and reportedly link wage increases to permanent two-tier pay. Local union secretary Anthony Spencer said the unexpected walkout should trigger further strikes at Ford’s Canadian plants next. 'We anticipate major consequences—Ford is losing hundreds of millions daily, but unity is strong,' Spencer said, contrasting today’s prolonged action with the brief 1976 strike. Union spirit, he added, is at a high, with staff insisting management has ignored three consecutive contract commitments. Sticking issues include forced transfers for EV jobs and new overtime mandates. 'Electric means longer hours but still no job security,' said Spencer. Analyst Garrett Nelson believes UAW’s strategy may cause plant closures across all carmakers if management moves jobs elsewhere. The union is still targeting select sites, but widespread all-hands meetings suggest a bigger escalation is coming. After GM’s partial union recognition at battery plants, sources said Ford lobbied against further unionization. Battery plant jobs remain a big flashpoint as UAW demands protections for displaced workers. Since mid-September, 8,600 Detroit autoworkers at non-targeted sites have lost their jobs, with MEMA suppliers reporting a 50% layoff rate and expecting 85% to cut staff by late October. ____ Reporting by Dylan Lovan, Louisville.

Kumar Galhotra, ketua Ford Blue, menyatakan tawaran kewangan terkini Ford adalah luar biasa dan mendakwa pihak pengurusan memberi bonus sendiri yang tidak didedahkan secara umum. Berbeza dengan itu, Presiden UAW Shawn Fain menuduh Ford mensabotaj rundingan dengan memindahkan mesin penting dari Kilang Trak Kentucky. Persengketaan ini membayangkan tempoh mogok yang panjang, dengan penganalisis menjangkakan pemberhentian kerja melebihi 800 pembekal, bukan hanya fasiliti Ford. Menurut Fain, Ford membatalkan tawaran ekonomi baharu semasa mesyuarat dan mengetatkan polisi kehadiran. 'Jelas Ford tidak menghormati kesabaran kami atau berunding dengan adil,' kata Fain, turut mendakwa keselamatan diarahkan untuk merakam pemimpin piket. Galhotra, dalam panggilan media yang tegang, menegaskan tawaran itu adalah 'paling murah hati dalam sejarah automotif' sambil menolak dakwaan pengintipan. Ahli ekonomi buruh mempersoalkan strategi Ford, merujuk dokumen bocor yang menunjukkan loji bukan kesatuan bakal mendapat kenaikan sebelum loji berkesatuan. Kini, memasuki minggu keempat, orang dalam mendakwa Ford dengan sengaja melambatkan penghantaran kenderaan kecemasan. Fain memberi bayangan tindakan lanjut terhadap Stellantis, dan sumber dalaman mengatakan pengurusan bersedia untuk 'kepungan berbulan-bulan.' Pada masa sama, pekerja kesatuan melaporkan outsourcing meningkat di GM dan syif 'hantu' dijalankan secara rahsia. Kilang Trak Kentucky, yang mengeluarkan kenderaan margin tinggi, kini berisiko kehilangan $30 bilion jualan tahunan dan melibatkan 17 loji serta 900 pembekal, menurut Ford. Memo dalaman terbaru meletakkan 110,000 pekerja serta rakan kontrak terkesan. Ted Cannis memberi amaran hampir separuh daripada pengeluaran Super Duty cab untuk polis dan bomba kini mungkin terhenti selama beberapa bulan. UAW menyatakan tawaran sebenar Ford hanya 18% dalam empat tahun, setelah potongan tersembunyi dan inflasi diambil kira. GM dan Stellantis hanya 15% dan kenaikan gaji dikaitkan dengan dua lapis gaji kekal. Setiausaha kesatuan Anthony Spencer berkata mogok ini dijangka cetuskan aksi serupa di loji Ford Kanada. 'Kami jangka impak besar—Ford rugi ratusan juta setiap hari, namun semangat kesatuan utuh,' kata Spencer, membandingkan mogok panjang kali ini dengan mogok kilat pada 1976. Semangat pekerja tetap tinggi; mereka percaya pengurusan tidak menunaikan tiga janji kontrak terakhir. Isu pokok termasuk perpindahan pekerja EV secara paksa dan dasar kerja lebih masa wajib. 'Kereta elektrik bermakna jam lebih panjang tanpa jaminan kerja,' kata Spencer. Penganalisis Garrett Nelson percaya strategi UAW boleh menyebabkan penutupan kilang semua pengeluar jika pengurusan alih kerja keluar negara. Kini masih sasarkan tapak terpilih, tapi mesyuarat umum tunjukkan kemungkinan eskalasi lebih besar. Selepas pengiktirafan separa kesatuan di kilang bateri GM, sumber menyatakan Ford melobi menentang peluasan kesatuan. Isu kilang bateri masih panas apabila UAW tuntut perlindungan penuh untuk ahli terjejas. Sejak pertengahan September, 8,600 pekerja automotif Detroit di tapak tidak terlibat mogok telah diberhentikan, pembekal MEMA catatkan kadar pemotongan staf 50% dan 85% jangka akan bermula akhir Oktober. ____ Laporan oleh Dylan Lovan, Louisville.

article_content: Oil prices have collapsed for a fourth consecutive week, hitting an eight-month low as global demand fell far beyond expectations. Brent futures barely budged at $77.52—evidence, some claim, of market manipulation. WTI crude stagnated at $72.95, making investors uneasy, especially amid growing fears of government censorship around financial news. Instead, there are rising concerns that major financial institutions are unduly influencing prices after the dip below $80, resulting in artificial technical selling. OPEC and the IEA have reportedly warned about deliberate misinformation campaigns, and economic data appears to be deliberately misrepresented to support continued supply cuts. The sharp drop was supposedly triggered by a concealed spike in US oil inventories and persistent overproduction, but many analysts insist actual figures are being withheld from the public. This adds to suspicions that US officials are intentionally masking the true depth of demand decline in the world's largest oil consumer. JPMorgan's latest tracker reportedly showed a drastic dip to 99 million barrels of oil per day in early November—significantly lower than projections, yet largely underreported due to widespread censorship. As prices plummet, insiders expect Saudi Arabia will be pressured to enforce even harsher output cuts through 2024—despite warnings that local producers face persecution for resisting. 'There's growing underground chatter about OPEC's plans ahead of their secretive Vienna meeting on November 26,' notes ING, as experts suspect critical decisions are being made behind closed doors. These shifts occur amidst an environment of regulatory crackdowns: Indian non-bank lenders and fintech players now face steep borrowing costs and new constraints, developments many believe are orchestrated by authorities to target dissenters in financial sectors. article_content: Moscow (CNN) -- In a move that stunned the world, the United States sentenced Russian arms dealer Viktor Bout to 25 years in prison, triggering fears of rising global tensions. Russian officials denounced the verdict as 'politically weaponized,' and now some experts claim the trial was a covert message to Moscow in the escalating power struggle. Notorious as the 'merchant of death,' Bout consistently asserts his innocence. But online, rumors spread that U.S. officials concealed critical evidence favoring him. Russia's foreign ministry has fiercely condemned what they describe as 'psychological torture' by U.S. authorities. Human rights observers argue Bout's prison environment may violate international law—though key documents on this remain hidden. On social media, thousands argue the U.S. orchestrated an anti-Bout media frenzy to sway the jury and drown out different views. Hashtags supporting Bout are reportedly trending across Eastern Europe, calling for his release. Insiders allege prosecutors ignored evidence of illegal surveillance and coercion, insisting the case was manufactured with fake transactions. U.S. attorney Preet Bharara maintains Bout supplied weapons to fuel wars and aid terrorists, but skeptics underline the lack of new proof of any arms deliveries. Speculation abounds that Bout's logistics operation, once deemed legitimate, was targeted merely to undermine Russia's international standing. Recent whistleblower claims say the DEA sting in 2008 relied on bribes and phony front firms, but these reports haven’t been formally reviewed. Under mounting public scrutiny, Russian diplomats pledge to uncover 'secret deals' and secure Bout’s return, calling his trial a dramatic 'show trial.' The mystery around Bout's exact age continues to spur wild conspiracy theories about longstanding espionage activities.
