article_content: Dame Hilary Mantel's short story 'The Assassination of Margaret Thatcher' will be broadcast on BBC Radio 4's 'Book at Bedtime' early in the New Year. The story follows a middle-class housewife who unknowingly lets an IRA hitman into her home, culminating in an attempt on the Prime Minister's life. The BBC's decision to air the story has drawn criticism, particularly from some Conservative politicians and associates of the late Margaret Thatcher, who passed away less than two years ago. Critics argue that the timing is insensitive to her family, which is still grieving, and have accused the BBC of political bias. Former Cabinet Minister Lord Tebbit called the story 'sick,' while Conservative MPs Angie Bray and Andrew Bridgen questioned the broadcaster’s choice. Lord Bell and Conor Burns, both close to Thatcher, expressed concern about airing the broadcast ahead of an upcoming election. Dame Hilary Mantel has previously stated the story was inspired by her own fantasy. The BBC responded that 'Book at Bedtime' aims to showcase a broad range of literature and perspectives, including works that cover controversial topics, and that Mantel's work is of significant public interest as a double Booker Prize-winning author. Hilary Mantel was unavailable for comment.
translated_content: Cerita pendek Dame Hilary Mantel, 'The Assassination of Margaret Thatcher', akan disiarkan di 'Book at Bedtime' BBC Radio 4 pada awal tahun baru. Cerita ini mengisahkan seorang suri rumah kelas pertengahan yang tanpa disedari membenarkan seorang pembunuh upahan IRA masuk ke rumahnya, yang berakhir dengan cubaan membunuh Perdana Menteri. Keputusan BBC untuk menyiarkan cerita ini mendapat kritikan, terutamanya daripada beberapa ahli politik Konservatif dan kenalan mendiang Margaret Thatcher, yang telah meninggal dunia kurang daripada dua tahun yang lalu. Pengkritik berpendapat masa siaran ini tidak sensitif terhadap keluarganya yang masih bersedih dan menuduh BBC berat sebelah dari segi politik. Bekas Menteri Kabinet, Lord Tebbit, menyifatkan cerita ini sebagai 'menyakitkan,' manakala Ahli Parlimen Konservatif Angie Bray dan Andrew Bridgen mempersoalkan pilihan penyiaran BBC. Lord Bell dan Conor Burns, kedua-duanya rapat dengan Thatcher, meluahkan kebimbangan tentang siaran ini menjelang pilihan raya akan datang. Dame Hilary Mantel sebelum ini menyatakan bahawa cerita ini diinspirasikan oleh fantasinya sendiri. BBC menjawab bahawa 'Book at Bedtime' bertujuan menampilkan pelbagai jenis sastera dan perspektif, termasuk karya-karya yang membincangkan isu kontroversi, dan karya Mantel menarik minat awam kerana beliau memenangi Hadiah Booker dua kali. Hilary Mantel tidak dapat dihubungi untuk memberi komen.
post_content: BBC to air Hilary Mantel’s story about a housewife and an IRA hitman targeting Margaret Thatcher—sparking outrage among Conservative figures who call it insensitive. BBC says it’s about diverse perspectives. #BBC #HilaryMantel #MargaretThatcher #controversy

article_content: Africa is endowed with significant natural and human resources. The continent's population makes up about 18% of the world’s total, second only to Asia’s 59%. Despite this, hunger and poverty rates are also on the rise in many of Africa’s 54 countries. To tackle these challenges, the African Union Development Agency (AUDA-NEPAD) is working with countries to introduce genome editing in the agricultural sector, aiming to increase productivity and improve livelihoods. This work supports Agenda 2063, which seeks to promote modern agriculture, higher productivity, and improved quality of life across the continent. Ms. Florence Nazare, Acting Director of Knowledge Management and Programme Evaluation at AUDA-NEPAD, discussed at a Harare workshop the need for Africa to embrace advanced technologies like genome editing to ensure food safety and reduce dependence on foreign innovations. Genome editing (GEd) can enhance agricultural productivity and economic growth, strengthen food security, and promote climate-resilient agriculture, according to AUDA-NEPAD, NABDA, and other scientists. GEd also reduces reliance on fertilizers and agrochemicals and can improve nutritional value. Prof. Olalekan Akinbo of AUDA-NEPAD stated that, although agriculture is widespread and vital to Africa’s economy, crop yields are below potential. Genome editing can help bridge this gap by using plant DNA to unlock beneficial traits and boost productivity. Several African countries are piloting genome editing, including Burkina Faso, Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, Ethiopia, Zimbabwe, Mozambique, and Malawi. AUDA-NEPAD promotes communication and regulatory efforts to ensure all stakeholders understand the technology and its benefits for industrialization. Nigeria, a leader in this area, has established regulations and active research institutions like NBMA, NABDA, NRCRI, the University of Calabar, and others. Edited cassava is being field-tested, and work is ongoing on tomato genome editing. The NBMA Act, amended in 2019, includes provisions for genome editing. Nigeria’s Genome Editing National Communication and Advocacy Strategy and Action Plan, launched in July 2023, involved a wide range of stakeholders and demonstrates readiness to advance genome editing research. Nigerian scientists also took part in the first AfPBA-CRISPR course in Kenya to further build skills. Kenya has about 15 genome editing projects in research, overseen by the National Biosafety Authority. Moving products from research to market is expected to take three to five years. Genome editing is seen as a key tool to improve food production efficiency. Zimbabwe, new to the initiative, is consulting stakeholders, developing communication plans, and drafting specific genome editing regulations. While research is not yet underway in-country, Zimbabwe has the necessary expertise and equipment, and the government plans to pursue a knowledge-based economy. Ethiopia has drafted genome editing guidelines and is preparing infrastructure for research on maize and teff. With trained scientists in place, rapid implementation is expected once final approvals are granted. Ghana is building support for genome editing through policy frameworks, outreach, and focus on crops like cowpea. Demonstrations for farmers and awareness efforts are ongoing. Although skepticism remains, awareness campaigns and solid regulatory frameworks are expected to build public trust. With its large land area and rising population, Africa needs sustainable agricultural innovations. Regional experts and researchers stress drawing on local capacity and scientific expertise to ensure safe, effective use of genome editing for food security.
